summary: Every process the global Linux gate runs, with the exit status it returned, what it proves about M4's surface, and what it does not. processes holds those and only those: it is reconciled against ravel:verify's own after list in nix/common.nix in both directions by verify_m4_process_matrix in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs, so a row the gate does not run and a gate sub-task with no row both fail the gate by name. checksOutsideTheGate holds what was run by hand instead, and no row there is a figure the command under gate produced. The figures under gate are the run evidence/m4/manifest.json records under commands and tests, and verify_m4_gate_figures refuses the two documents when they disagree.

gameLaunch.whyItIsNotHere: M4 is the SDK breadth milestone and every surface it added is exercised inside the gate. No game process was started for it, so nothing recorded here observes Ravel inside Minecraft. That is a field rather than a sentence because it is the single most misreadable thing about this record: M3's matrix of the same name is an operator-run native launch, and this one is not. What a launch would add is the half nothing here reaches — a mod discovered from a package, a declared side honoured by a host inside the game rather than by the harness that stands in for it, a packet crossing a connection — and each of those is recorded as an owed obligation in evidence/m4/manifest.json rather than as a gap this record closes.
gameLaunch.whatWouldChangeIt: A launch campaign of the shape M3-W7 ran. It needs an operator, the display, and the pinned local fixture, and no M4 work package owns one.

resultCeiling: A reader can recompute every row below by running the named command on a checkout with the devenv shell. That is the whole of what this record attests, and it is deliberately more recomputable and less far-reaching than M3's matrix: every row under processes is a gate process, so the matrix proves the gate passes and proves nothing about a running game. The one row that is not a gate process is under checksOutsideTheGate and is labelled as such, because a table headed by ravel:verify's exit status must not carry a row that command never ran.
measuredAgainst: a clean working copy at the head of the change stack that lands M4's evidence. Every row below was run individually, in the order listed, on that tree. evidence/m4/manifest.json pins revision.id at the change that introduced it, which is below that head by construction: recording a result changes the tree that produced it, so no evidence record can pin the tree it was measured on and also be part of it. The manifest states the same ceiling as a deviation rather than leaving it to be discovered. The figures here were re-measured after the first round of M4-W8's independent review and the repairs answering it, because those repairs added checks and therefore tests: a recorded run that no longer describes the tree it is bound to is the stale figure this record spends its checks preventing.

coverage.source: the Lines, Regions and Functions columns of cargo llvm-cov's own summary, taken from the same invocation ravel:coverage runs, with the experiments/adg- filename filter that task applies

processes.proves: Rust, Nix, shell, TOML, JSON and Markdown in the tree are formatted, which covers the author's guide M4-W7 added as well as the code.
processes.doesNotProve: Anything about what the documents say.

processes.proves: The workspace type-checks with all features, and the tracked JSON documents validate against the schemas under schemas/, which is where a package manifest's grammar is decided.
processes.doesNotProve: That a manifest validating against the schema describes a mod any launch will load. At the recorded run nothing in a launch path read a package manifest at all; the composed host was given manifests to admit its members from after this milestone closed, and even then only the manifests compiled in beside the code, so nothing here reaches a manifest a launch discovered.

processes.proves: clippy::all and clippy::pedantic pass with no allow escape hatches, across the SDK crates M4 filled in.
processes.doesNotProve: That the API a lint-clean crate exposes is one an author can use; the guide and the fresh-author run are what tested that.

processes.proves: Every unit and conformance test passes, including the M4 suites for content declarations, sides and packets, config and saves and services, pack closure, the example package, the SDK author boundary and every compiled snippet in the guide.
processes.doesNotProve: That any of those surfaces is reached by a running game. Each suite drives the loader's own pipeline in-process.

processes.proves: Workspace line coverage is at or above the floor the task fixes, measured over the same run that produced the figures under gate.coverage.
processes.doesNotProve: That any particular crate or file is covered; the floor is a workspace figure and nothing in the gate reads a per-file percentage.

processes.proves: The repository scaffold holds, the tracked-file policy holds, and every milestone manifest — this one included — is schema-valid, digest-bound, provenance-checked and internally consistent in its arithmetic.
processes.doesNotProve: Whether any milestone is closed. That is ravel:verify-milestone, and for M4 it exits nonzero by design while the milestone is open.

processes.surface: pack example, written to disk and compared against two independent lists
processes.proves: The M4-W5 pack example runs as its own process, writes a pack, and the tree it wrote matches both the file list the gate holds independently and the example's own report of what it wrote.
processes.doesNotProve: That Ravel reads a written pack. The gate reads the tree with find and jq; no Ravel code path in this repository consumes a written pack, and M8 owns the half that would.

processes.proves: cargo xtask package digests --check finds the minimal example's manifest digests current against the files beside them, which is the M4-W7 packaging tool exercised on the package an author is told to copy.
processes.doesNotProve: That everything a manifest declares is protected. Only source.files and the provenance record are integrity-checked, so anything declared elsewhere and not also listed there is checked by nothing here or anywhere.

processes.proves: The M1 spike results still satisfy the gates they were recorded against.
processes.doesNotProve: Anything about M4; this row is here because it is part of the global gate M4-W8 has to pass, not because M4 added to it.

processes.proves: Every tracked version's generated Java is put through javac under -Xlint:all -Werror, and every screen class is loaded by the name that version's ScreenNames records. Before this existed nothing compiled any version but the one the shell selects, so an obfuscated version's screens, stubs, GameNames and ScreenNames were generated, byte-compared and never seen by a compiler.
processes.doesNotProve: That the compiled classes link against the real game. The stubs are the game at compile time and the stub tree is deliberately never packaged, so a flat stub standing in for a nested type models no nestmate access and a class can compile here and fail to link there. The screens are loaded from an ordinary class path with the stubs on it, not through Instrumentation.appendToSystemClassLoaderSearch against an already-loaded game, which is the loader a launch uses. A version whose published mapping is absent is skipped rather than compiled, and target/ravel-jvm/compiled-versions.txt is what says which versions were actually compiled.

processes.proves: Ravel's agent and its persistence adapter run inside a real JVM process, over stand-in classes, through every world lifecycle the harness declares.
processes.doesNotProve: That the adapter's reflective surface matches the game's. Both sides of the harness are Ravel's own — Ravel's stubs asserted against Ravel's reflection — so a game-side rename would keep it passing. That surface is unpinned and is recorded as an owed obligation in evidence/m4/manifest.json.

processes.proves: The recorded M2 and M3 budgets still compare as they were recorded to.
processes.doesNotProve: Anything M4 measured. M4 added no performance limit.

processes.proves: cargo deny finds no advisory, licence, ban or source violation across the dependency graph the SDK's closure resolves.
processes.doesNotProve: That the closure is small enough for an author to reason about; the SDK boundary suite is what states the closure.

processes.proves: Every change in the stack carries a conventional description and the working copy is not carrying undescribed work.
processes.doesNotProve: Anything about the content of a change. It fails on any dirty tree in tens of milliseconds, which is why it cannot be the task that judges whether some other check caught a mutation.

checksOutsideTheGate.whyItIsNotAGateProcess: ravel:verify does not run it. ROADMAP.md distinguishes the two gates in as many words — ravel:verify is the fast code-policy graph and ravel:verify-environment runs devenv test and nix flake check — and nix/common.nix's after list for ravel:verify does not name it. This row was written among the processes above in the first draft of this record, which made the record claim the gate had run a process it had not; the M4-W8 independent review's first round found that and it is separated here. verify_m4_process_matrix in tools/ravel-xtask/src/lib.rs now reconciles the processes array against that after list in both directions and requires every row in this section to name a task the gate does not run.
checksOutsideTheGate.proves: The devenv environment builds and its own checks pass, so the commands above are reproducible from the pinned environment rather than from whatever was on the machine. It was run by hand for this record.
checksOutsideTheGate.doesNotProve: Anything about the gate. Nothing in devenv tasks run ravel:verify reaches this task, so a red result here does not make the gate red and a green one is not a gate figure. It also does not prove reproducibility on a different hardware profile; every figure recorded here is from linux-reference-v1.

whatAGreenMatrixDoesNotSay: That a mod can send a packet. Nothing in Ravel carries a mod's packet to the other end; the encode and decode halves are what these rows exercise.

That a mod's declared sides are honoured. The shipped host read no manifest at the recorded run, so no row here observed a side declaration having an effect. That was repaired after the milestone closed and the JVM harness row now does observe it, which is a fact about the tree rather than about this record; what stays true of every row is that none of them is a game process.
That a written pack can be read back. No row reads one with Ravel.
That a general crate runs against the second version's target table. The version rows prove a generator run and a name sweep, and one build compiles one table.
redaction: No launcher path, instance path, account, world name or user path appears in this record, and none was needed: every row is a repository-relative command run inside the devenv shell.
